flashcard_questions.q: What does electrolysis do to an ionic compound?
flashcard_questions.a: It uses an electric current to decompose it into its elements.

flashcard_questions.q: Why must an electrolyte be molten or dissolved?
flashcard_questions.a: The ions must be free to move and carry the current.

flashcard_questions.q: Which electrode is called the cathode in electrolysis?
What happens to positive ions when they reach the cathode?
flashcard_questions.a: They gain electrons and are reduced.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to negative ions when they reach the anode?
flashcard_questions.a: They lose electrons and are oxidised.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis rather than reduction with carbon?
flashcard_questions.a: It is too reactive to be displaced by carbon.

flashcard_questions.q: Which ore is the main source of aluminium?
Why is aluminium oxide dissolved in molten cryolite?
flashcard_questions.a: It lowers the melting point to about 950 °C, cutting energy costs.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do the graphite anodes in aluminium extraction burn away?
flashcard_questions.a: They react with the oxygen produced to form carbon dioxide.

flashcard_questions.q: When is hydrogen produced at the cathode of an aqueous solution?
flashcard_questions.a: When the metal is more reactive than hydrogen.

flashcard_questions.q: When is oxygen produced at the anode of an aqueous solution?
flashcard_questions.a: When no halide ions are present in the solution.

flashcard_questions.q: Which gas forms at the cathode when brine is electrolysed?
Which gas forms at the anode when brine is electrolysed?
Which solution is left in the cell after brine is electrolysed?
(Higher) What is the anode half equation for chloride ions?
